newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Mexico's TMM downgraded.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Mexico's TMM downgraded.

text.p: -- Bear Stearns analyst Santiago Pique said the brokerage was downgrading the rating on Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) to neutral from attractive to reflect the near term dilutive effect of the recently awarded concession for the Northeast railway line.

-- "We are revising our 1997 EPS estimates to $0.61 from $0.84. Based on the company's projections and our own estimates we calculate the 1997 impact of the rail concession at a negative $0.23 per share," he added.
-- Pique said given the dilutive effect of the rail venture and continuing margin pressures affecting the Far East route, "we see little near-term upside potential in the TMM stock."

-- "If the company's projected growth scenario materializes, the rail concession could potentially provide incremental earnings per share of $0.77 on year three, growing to $1.48 by year five," Pique added.
-- "We continue to consider TMM an attractive investment over the longer term and will carefully monitor the company's progress against its stated growth objective for the rail subsidiary," he said.

TMM and its partner Kansas City Southern Industries Inc, through its subsidiary Transportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana, was awarded a 50-year concession to operate the Northeast rail line of the recently privatized rail system.
